issues.title: KM relaxation condition has an unbound summation index
issues.failure_explanation: The relaxation sequence is indexed by k, but the displayed series binds n and repeatedly uses the free term λ_k. Taken literally, it does not impose divergence of the series formed from the parameter sequence. The admissible restriction λ_k∈(0,1] does not repair this indexing failure.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory statement of the classical variable-parameter KM condition is malformed. The paper's later lemma states the condition correctly, so no TKMA formal result depends on this occurrence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: At TradKMcond, replace the free subscript by the bound one, for example by writing ∑_{n=1}^{∞} λ_n(1−λ_n)=∞; equivalently, rename the dummy index consistently throughout the series.
issues.why_classification: The surrounding text concerns the sequence {λ_k}, and lem:KMthm states the same divergence condition with a consistently bound index. The possible edits are mathematically equivalent dummy-index renamings, and no argument or TKMA result depends on this malformed introductory occurrence.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: extended in \cite{groetsch1972note} to variable parameters under the condition $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lambda_k(1-\lambda_k)=+\infty$

issues.title: Proximity-operator construction names the wrong function

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $\psi\in\Gamma_{0}(\mD)$, the proximity operator of $\psi$ at $\bmx\in\mD$ is defined by

issues.failure_explanation: The construction's declared input function and minimization objective are ψ, whereas the output operator is named prox_f, with f already denoting a different objective term. For f≠ψ, the displayed contract associates the computed minimizer with the wrong function and leaves the intended prox_ψ notation inconsistent.
issues.overall_effect: The proximity-operator interface is internally inconsistent and compromises the literal prox_ψ notation used by secproxthm and the subsequent fixed-point construction, although the intended operator is immediately recoverable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the definition's left-hand label from prox_f(x) to prox_ψ(x), leaving the minimization objective unchanged. This defines exactly the operator denoted in secproxthm and the subsequent fixed-point formulas.
issues.why_classification: The introducing sentence, the quantifier ψ∈Γ₀(D), and the minimand ψ uniquely force the subscript ψ, while f denotes a different function. Correcting the label changes neither the computed minimizer nor any mathematical inference, so the defect is transcriptional.

issues.title: Proximity lemma places its convexity hypothesis on the wrong function
issues.failure_explanation: The old lemma quantifies f∈Γ₀(D), while both ∂ψ and prox_ψ in its conclusion concern ψ. No equality f=ψ is imposed, so the lemma's own hypotheses do not bind the function to which the subdifferential/proximity equivalence is applied. This also fails to formally license the subsequent instantiation with ψ=φ/λ.
issues.overall_effect: The stated auxiliary lemma is under-hypothesized and does not formally justify the FPPA derivation at partial3, although its intended reading is unambiguous.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis “Let f∈Γ₀(D)” in secproxthm by “Let ψ∈Γ₀(D),” and apply the corrected lemma at partial3 with ψ=φ/λ. Since λ>0 and φ is proper lower-semicontinuous convex, the remainder of the FPPA derivation is unchanged.
issues.why_classification: As written, the regularity assumption on f supplies no premise for the function ψ appearing in the conclusion, so the subsequent application is not formally licensed. The repair is nevertheless a short, standard, source-forced correction that preserves the exact lemma and derivation without a new argument or any mathematical loss.

issues.title: Residual square-summability item uses a vacuous inequality
issues.failure_explanation: The assertion that the nonnegative series is ≤+∞ permits the value +∞ and therefore does not state summability. In contrast, Seriesineq, together with η>0 and a finite squared norm on its right-hand side, proves that the series is strictly finite. Consequently, the printed item also cannot supply the finite-summability premise cited in the proof of convergerate.
issues.overall_effect: Item (i) of thm:conv fails to record the estimate actually proved, and the rate proof's stated reliance on that item is invalid as written. The estimate needed for both results is nevertheless already present in the old proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace “∑_{k=0}^{∞}‖Tx^k−x^k‖²≤+∞” in thm:conv(i) by the strict finiteness statement “∑_{k=0}^{∞}‖Tx^k−x^k‖²<+∞.” The existing Seriesineq proves this because η>0 and its right-hand side is finite; the corrected item then supplies the premise used in convergerate.
issues.why_classification: The literal item is vacuous, and the rate proof relies on the stronger finite-summability meaning, so the affected chain contains a genuine logical support defect rather than an unused typographical blemish. However, the required estimate is already explicitly proved, making the complete repair local and routine with no new lemma, rate change, or other loss.

issues.title: Finite experiments are claimed to certify infinite summability

failure_location.quote: This experimentally verifies that the condition $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} |\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|<+\infty$ in Theorem \ref{convergerate} is satisfied in the denoising scenario, thereby ensuring the convergence rate of TKMA as established by the theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\sum_{k=0}^{n} |\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|$ for TKMA against the iteration count $n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old prose claims that the plot verifies convergence of the infinite series and thereby ensures TKMA's theorem-level rate in the denoising scenario. What the old paper actually establishes is a conditional rate theorem together with a plot of finite partial sums through computed iteration counts. A finite prefix or apparent trend cannot establish behavior of the entire unobserved tail, so the experiment supplies heuristic evidence rather than certification of the hypothesis or guarantee of the rate.
issues.overall_effect: The conditional theorem remains unaffected, but the claimed applicability of its rate guarantee to the denoising experiments is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the certification language by a statement that the plotted finite partial sums exhibit an apparent stabilization and provide empirical evidence consistent with possible convergence of the infinite series, but do not verify that convergence or ensure the theorem's rate in the denoising scenario. Keep convergerate as a conditional theorem; a categorical application would require an independent tail estimate.
issues.why_classification: Serious: the recorded complete repair withdraws both the claimed certification of infinite summability in the denoising scenario and the resulting theorem-level rate guarantee for that scenario. Finite empirical observations consistent with summability do not preserve a comparable guarantee of either claim. Retaining the conditional theorem does not restore its advertised certified applicability. This is major loss of the affected prose guarantee despite a local correction and no change to the conditional proof. An independent tail estimate is a stated obligation, not an established guarantee-restoring repair in the record; the classification does not assert that such an estimate could never be proved.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: The observed convergence trend of the partial sums provides empirical evidence that the infinite series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} |\theta_{k+1}-\theta_k|$ may be bounded in the denoising scenario. This result aligns with the theoretical condition in Theorem \ref{convergerate} and offers experimental support for the convergence rate of TKMA established therein.
